02_automl_and_resource_constraints.title: Selection stability under budget constraints
02_automl_and_resource_constraints.caption: Checks the stability of candidate selection and calibrated operating points. The primary combined recall/FPR requirement was not reliably met.

03_cross_dataset_transfer.title: Transfer threshold-gate feasibility
03_cross_dataset_transfer.caption: Tests whether transferred scores support the declared recall and false-positive budgets. Failed operating points remain visible; threshold control alone is insufficient.

03_cross_dataset_transfer.title: Transfer risk by capture
03_cross_dataset_transfer.caption: Separates capture-specific recall and false alarms rather than treating pooled performance as deployment safety.

04_temporal_adaptation.title: CSE adaptation across capture days
04_temporal_adaptation.caption: Compares daily F1 across frozen and update policies. Performance varies by capture; a pooled adaptation gain does not establish uniform safety.

04_temporal_adaptation.title: Threshold recalibration, seed 42
04_temporal_adaptation.caption: Shows the recall/false-alarm tradeoff from threshold-only changes. Recalibration is distinct from improving the score ranking.

04_temporal_adaptation.title: Threshold recalibration across two seeds
04_temporal_adaptation.caption: Checks whether the same-stream tradeoff changes with model seed. Repeated seeds are not independent-network validation.

04_temporal_adaptation.title: Smart-factory chronological replay
04_temporal_adaptation.caption: Compares policies over successive chunks. A low-FPR policy can still lose useful attack detections; family and chunk behavior must accompany pooled metrics.

04_temporal_adaptation.title: APEX frozen-model replay
04_temporal_adaptation.caption: Measures fixed-model behavior across temporal segments. This is additional development evidence, not a successful adaptation or independent-confirmation claim.

05_delayed_feedback_and_safeguards.title: Validate-before-commit comparison
05_delayed_feedback_and_safeguards.caption: Evaluates source-method admission and an FPR-oriented gate on a shared campaign. This is a same-stream development comparison; label-evidence budgets are not fully matched.

07_generalization_and_context.title: Context representation ablation
07_generalization_and_context.caption: Separates representation effects across chronological windows and selection rules. Context additions do not automatically restore feasibility.

07_generalization_and_context.title: Matched multi-environment fitting
07_generalization_and_context.caption: Compares training exposure under matched conditions. Nearby-period gains do not guarantee later-period low-FPR generalization.

07_generalization_and_context.title: Low-FPR ranking limits
07_generalization_and_context.caption: Uses retrospective labels to diagnose recall achievable from fitted scores at fixed FPR. These thresholds are not deployable or used for protected tuning.

07_generalization_and_context.title: Service, direction and protocol context
07_generalization_and_context.caption: Compares causal contextual representations with the flow baseline. None of these contextual variants restored the required later-period joint operating point.

07_generalization_and_context.title: Full-density contextual tail risk
07_generalization_and_context.caption: Shows how errors vary over real chronological windows. Worst-window false alarms can remain severe even when pooled metrics look less extreme.

08_behavioral_detection.title: Full behavioral detector comparison
08_behavioral_detection.caption: Six frozen pipelines score 9,160,253 development flows. The hybrid raises recall to 90.27% but also raises FPR to 8.68%; this fails the deployment operating point.

08_behavioral_detection.title: Behavioral false alarms over time
08_behavioral_detection.caption: Separates supported-minute FPR and recall across the replay. Behavioral/hybrid detectors can have extreme localized false alarms despite high pooled recall.

08_behavioral_detection.title: Fitting-family coverage ablation
08_behavioral_detection.caption: With ToN DDoS excluded from fitting, the hybrid retains strong nearby recall while the flow baseline drops. This local finding fails to generalize to the later stress period and is not proof of zero-day detection.

09_data_integrity_and_observability.title: ToN hourly campaign composition
09_data_integrity_and_observability.caption: Establishes chronological attack-family and benign-support changes. This is a data-composition audit, not classifier accuracy or proof of natural production drift.

09_data_integrity_and_observability.title: WUSTL temporal label distribution
09_data_integrity_and_observability.caption: Screens whether class support and chronology permit the intended evaluation. Dataset suitability is a separate question from model quality.

09_data_integrity_and_observability.title: APEX temporal and feature availability
09_data_integrity_and_observability.caption: Audits timeline/feature availability before replay. Availability artifacts must be distinguished from learned attack behavior.

09_data_integrity_and_observability.title: Reconnaissance pulse diagnostic
09_data_integrity_and_observability.caption: Examines the relationship between campaign composition and errors. A concentrated pulse can distort pooled estimates; it is not a newly invented attack detector.

09_data_integrity_and_observability.title: Scanning observability on the fixed fitting sample
09_data_integrity_and_observability.caption: Measures label-assisted lookup optima for several recorded representations on the same fitting sample. Sample ceilings are not future guarantees; see the separate full-prefix audit.

09_data_integrity_and_observability.title: Raw-text full-prefix scanning bound
09_data_integrity_and_observability.caption: Audits 13,760,005 permitted training records. At 0.1% empirical FPR, complete recorded static descriptors permit at most 4.68% scanning recall. This is a family-specific empirical bound, not overall-IDS impossibility.
